rbc.name: RBC Royal Bank
rbc.tagline: Canada's largest bank, powering homeownership coast to coast.
rbc.overview: RBC Royal Bank is Canada's largest bank and a dominant force in the residential mortgage market. Known for stability, competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates, and a vast branch network, RBC serves millions of Canadian homeowners. Their mortgage offerings include fixed-rate mortgages, variable-rate mortgages, and the RBC Homeline Plan â€” a flexible home equity line of credit that lets you borrow up to 65% of your home's value. RBC offers online mortgage pre-approval with rate holds up to 120 days, making it easy to shop with confidence. Whether you're a first-time homebuyer navigating the stress test or a seasoned investor, RBC's mortgage advisors provide tailored guidance across Canada.
uniqueFeatures: RBC Homeline Plan for equity access

td.name: TD Bank
td.tagline: Comfortable banking with flexible mortgage solutions.
td.seoTitle: TD Mortgage Rates Canada | Fixed, Variable & Refinance
td.seoDescription: See current TD mortgage rates for a purchase or refinance. Compare fixed and variable TD Mortgage Solutions, then check how they stack up today.
td.overview:
TD Bank (Toronto-Dominion) is one of Canada's Big Five banks and a full-service mortgage lender with a large branch and digital network. Most shoppers meet TD as a direct lender: you apply with a mortgage specialist, online, or through an existing TD relationship rather than treating it as a broker-only monoline. The product set covers closed fixed and variable mortgages, refinances, and the TD Home Equity FlexLine, which pairs a traditional mortgage portion with a revolving home-equity line of credit.

TD is often chosen for convenience and prepayment flexibility (commonly cited as increasing payments by up to 100% and making annual lump-sum prepayments up to 15% of the original principal—confirm the current product sheet). It is less often the cheapest 5-year rate on a blind comparison against monolines. Use the live table on this page as the rate source; do not treat marketing copy as a quote. Then check GDS and TDS with the stress test calculator before you rely on a pre-approval.
td.whoItsFor:
TD mortgages tend to fit borrowers who already bank at TD, want in-person specialists, or need a bundled setup (chequing, credit cards, and a mortgage in one institution). The FlexLine is aimed at homeowners who want to keep unused equity available without a separate refinance every time they need funds.

TD is a weaker fit if your only goal is the lowest advertised 5-year rate and you are happy using a broker and a monoline. Big-bank credit, income, and property rules still apply, including the federal qualifying-rate test on new purchases and refinances. Newcomers with limited Canadian credit should ask specifically about TD's newcomer documentation—not assume every branch will structure the same deal.

products.title: Closed fixed-rate mortgages
products.description: Payment stays the same for the term (commonly 1–5 years, sometimes longer). Useful if you want a known payment and are comparing the 5-year fixed market. IRD or three-month interest penalties can apply if you break early.

products.title: Closed variable-rate mortgages
products.description: Rate moves with TD's prime. Your payment or the split between principal and interest will change with prime, depending on product. Still qualified at the stress-test rate, not at prime minus a discount.

products.title: TD Home Equity FlexLine
products.description: A readvanceable-style product: a mortgage segment plus a HELOC segment, typically capped by combined loan-to-value rules (often discussed as up to 80% combined, with the revolving portion limited further). Confirm current LTV caps with TD; they are policy, not a promise on this page.

products.title: Refinance and switch
products.description: TD can refinance an existing mortgage (subject to qualification) or receive a switch. Switching in from another lender is a new origination for stress-test purposes. Run the refinance calculator before you pay a penalty to move.

td.howRatesCompare:
TD's posted rates are not the rates most qualified borrowers pay. Special or discounted offers are what belong in a comparison. The cards and matrix at the top of this page are pulled from our rate feed—use those figures, not a round number from an old article.

On a vanilla 5-year closed mortgage, TD often sits with other large banks: convenient, relationship-priced, and frequently a bit higher than aggressive monolines. That gap can shrink if you have a strong TD relationship, a high-ratio insured deal, or a FlexLine structure the bank wants to book. Always compare the same term, insured vs uninsured, and the same prepayment rules. Start with 5-year fixed and variable hubs, then return here to see only TD's lineup.
shoppingTips: Ask for the discounted rate in writing (term, insured vs uninsured, and whether cash-back is attached). Posted rate is a starting point, not the deal.
If you hold other TD products, ask whether relationship pricing applies—and what happens to the rate if you later move your chequing account.
Map FlexLine fees, HELOC prime spread, and the split between the term mortgage and the line of credit before you choose it over a simple closed mortgage.
At renewal, get TD's offer first, then compare it to the live table on our homepage. Staying can skip a new stress test; switching usually cannot.
Confirm current prepayment privileges on the exact product (the widely cited 15% lump sum and 100% payment increase are not universal across every TD mortgage vintage).
Run GDS/TDS yourself with the stress test calculator using TD's offered contract rate, then compare the actual payment with the mortgage payment calculator.

faqs.question: Does TD usually have the lowest mortgage rate in Canada?
faqs.answer: Often no. TD is a full-service bank. On a plain 5-year closed mortgage, monoline lenders and some credit unions frequently advertise lower contract rates. TD can still win on convenience, FlexLine structure, or a relationship discount. Compare the live TD rates on this page with the 5-year fixed and variable hubs rather than assuming a bank rate is the market low.

faqs.question: What is the TD Home Equity FlexLine?
faqs.answer: It combines a traditional mortgage portion with a revolving home equity line of credit. You pay down the mortgage segment and, subject to the product rules, can re-borrow available credit without a brand-new application each time. Combined loan-to-value limits apply. It is more flexible than a simple closed mortgage and more complex to compare on rate alone.

faqs.question: Can I get a TD mortgage through a mortgage broker?
faqs.answer: TD is primarily a direct-to-consumer bank. Many brokers cannot book TD the way they book monolines. If you want TD specifically, plan to talk to a TD mortgage specialist or apply through TD's own channels, then still compare the offer against brokered lenders.

faqs.question: What prepayment privileges does TD advertise?
faqs.answer: TD commonly describes the ability to increase regular payments by up to 100% and to make lump-sum prepayments of up to 15% of the original principal each year, without a penalty. Privileges are product-specific and can differ on older books, cash-back mortgages, or promotions. Read the commitment letter.

faqs.question: Does TD offer mortgages for newcomers to Canada?
faqs.answer: TD has newcomer-focused mortgage programs that can use alternative documentation when Canadian credit history is thin. Eligibility, down-payment, and income rules are set by TD and by default insurers on high-ratio deals. Bring immigration status, foreign credit, and down-payment source documents to a specialist rather than relying on a website summary.

faqs.question: Should I renew with TD or switch lenders?
faqs.answer: Renewing with TD usually avoids a new stress test. Switching to another lender generally means qualifying again at the qualifying rate. If you would pass the stress test and another lender's rate is meaningfully lower after penalties and fees, switching can pay. If you are tight on GDS/TDS, TD's renewal offer may be the practical path even if it is not the lowest advertised rate.

scotiabank.name: Scotiabank
scotiabank.tagline: Unlock your home's potential with the Scotia Total Equity Plan.
scotiabank.overview: Scotiabank stands out in the Canadian mortgage market with its innovative Scotia Total Equity Plan (STEP), allowing homeowners to combine a mortgage with a home equity line of credit and access up to 80% of their home's value. Scotiabank offers competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates, plus specialized products for newcomers, self-employed borrowers, and investors. Their eHOME platform enables a fully digital mortgage application experience, while Home Financing Advisors provide personalized support in-branch or virtually. Scotia Mortgage Protection offers optional insurance coverage for life, disability, critical illness, and job loss â€” giving homeowners peace of mind.

With competitive rates, a user-friendly online mortgage calculator, and access to mortgage specialists across Canada, BMO helps borrowers navigate the mortgage stress test and find the right financing solution.

cibc.name: CIBC

CIBC provides fixed-rate, variable-rate, and convertible mortgages, along with specialized products for newcomers to Canada and investment properties. Their online mortgage tools, including payment calculators and pre-approval, make it easy to explore options from anywhere. CIBC mortgage advisors offer personalized advice with no cost or obligation, helping clients understand prepayment options and mortgage renewal strategies.
uniqueFeatures: Home Power Plan: mortgage + HELOC combo

nationalbank.name: National Bank of Canada

National Bank offers a full range of mortgage products including fixed-rate, variable-rate, and all-in-one banking solutions that combine mortgage and line of credit features. With competitive rates, a strong digital platform, and dedicated mortgage advisors, National Bank serves first-time buyers, renewals, refinances, and investors with tailored financing solutions.
uniqueFeatures: Flex Mortgage: split fixed and variable

nesto.name: nesto

For tech-savvy homebuyers seeking transparency and speed, nesto is a top choice.

simplii.name: Simplii Financial

Their mortgage calculators and educational resources help first-time buyers understand affordability and payment options.

tangerine.name: Tangerine
tangerine.tagline: Forward-thinking mortgages from Canada's original digital bank.
tangerine.overview: Tangerine, a subsidiary of Scotiabank, is one of Canada's most trusted digital banks, offering competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates with no hidden fees. Tangerine mortgages come with flexible features including annual prepayment options and the ability to increase regular payments. Their fully online mortgage application process is simple and fast, supported by a dedicated team of mortgage account managers. Tangerine is particularly popular among rate-conscious borrowers who appreciate transparent pricing and the backing of Scotiabank's financial strength. With mortgage rate specials, renewal offers, and a suite of digital tools, Tangerine makes home financing accessible and hassle-free.

eqbank.name: EQ Bank

EQ Bank's digital-first platform provides a seamless experience for mortgage pre-approval, rate comparison, and application. Their mortgages feature flexible terms, competitive fixed and variable rates, and no monthly banking fees. For borrowers seeking an alternative to the Big Six banks without sacrificing service, EQ Bank delivers a refreshing, tech-forward approach to Canadian mortgages.

alterna.name: Alterna Savings

Their mortgage specialists work closely with borrowers to find solutions tailored to individual needs, whether you're buying your first home, renewing, or refinancing. Alterna's digital banking platform makes managing your mortgage simple and convenient.

firstnational.name: First National Financial
firstnational.tagline: Canada's largest non-bank mortgage lender, exclusively through brokers.

First National offers some of the most competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates in Canada, with flexible prepayment options and exceptional customer service. Their My Mortgage online portal lets borrowers manage payments, view statements, and access mortgage details 24/7. First National is also a leader in commercial mortgages and multi-unit residential financing. For borrowers working with a mortgage broker, First National consistently delivers low rates, fast approvals, and industry-leading technology.

manulife.name: Manulife Bank
manulife.tagline: All-in-one banking that puts your mortgage to work.
manulife.seoTitle: Manulife Bank Mortgage Rates | Manulife One & Posted 2026
manulife.seoDescription: Compare Manulife Bank mortgage rates and Manulife One. See posted fixed and variable offers plus the all-in-one account, then check today's rates.
manulife.overview:
Manulife Bank is a Schedule I Canadian bank and a subsidiary of Manulife Financial. It is not a mortgage-only monoline. The distinctive product is Manulife One: an all-in-one account that can combine a mortgage, a line of credit, and day-to-day deposits so interest is charged on the net borrowed balance after you deposit income. Manulife also sells more conventional Manulife Bank Select fixed and variable mortgages for borrowers who want a standard closed term without operating their chequing account inside the mortgage.

Shop Manulife if the all-in-one structure matches how you actually hold cash. If you only want the lowest 5-year sticker rate and will keep a separate chequing account at another bank, start with the live rates on this page and still compare 5-year fixed offers from other lenders. For a different all-in-one style product, see Scotiabank's STEP.
manulife.whoItsFor:
Manulife One is built for people who will park paycheques, savings, and idle cash in the same account as the mortgage. Interest is calculated on the outstanding net balance, so a large deposit can cut interest in a way a conventional closed mortgage cannot. Households with lumpy income (bonuses, commission, or a sale proceeds parked temporarily) sometimes use that feature on purpose.

Skip One if you spend down to a low balance every month, want the simplest possible mortgage, or dislike mixing daily banking with your home loan. In that case look at Manulife Bank Select or another conventional lender. Manulife Bank is OSFI-regulated, so new purchases and refinances still need to pass the mortgage stress test.

products.title: Manulife One (all-in-one)
products.description: A readvanceable account: deposits reduce the balance that interest is charged on; you can hold variable and, depending on the setup, fixed-rate sub-accounts. Savings come from cash behaviour, not from a magic rate. Fees, sub-account rules, and the base rate are set by Manulife—read the current product page rather than old blog math.

products.title: Manulife Bank Select (conventional)
products.description: Standard closed fixed and variable mortgages if you want a familiar term, payment, and separate chequing account. Compare these first if you are rate-shopping against banks and monolines on a like-for-like 5-year closed product.

products.title: Variable and prime-linked options
products.description: Variable Select and One's base/variable components move with Manulife Bank's prime or base rate, not with a rate you lock for five years. Qualification still uses the stress-test rate, which is higher than the contract rate.

products.title: Home equity access
products.description: One's line-of-credit behaviour is the main way Manulife packages re-borrowing. Conventional HELOC-style access still has combined LTV limits. It is not a substitute for a refinance calculator if you are debt-consolidating a different lender.

manulife.howRatesCompare:
Manulife publishes posted tables and separate special or high-ratio offers. The figures in the cards above come from our feed—use them instead of any rate written in this article. Posted Select rates are often higher than the specials; One's headline savings are partly behavioural (cash sitting against the balance) and partly the contract rate on each sub-account.

On a straight 5-year closed comparison, Manulife is not automatically cheaper than a monoline. Where One can win is total interest over a few years if you genuinely keep a high average deposit. Where it can lose is if the contract rate is higher and your operating balance is thin. Compare insured vs uninsured lines in the matrix, then check variable and insured hubs for context.
shoppingTips: Decide first: Manulife One versus a conventional Select mortgage. Mixing the sales pitch from one product with the rate from the other is how people mis-shop this lender.
Ask for the current Manulife One base rate, any fixed sub-account rates, account fees, and how interest is calculated day-to-day—then model your real average balance, not a best-case month.
If you only want a closed 5-year, compare Select (or another lender) on term, insured vs uninsured, and prepayment penalties. Do not assume One is 'always less interest.'
Treat special 'as low as' rates as offer-sheet items with conditions (new clients, high-ratio, term). Match them to the same row in the table on this page.
Manulife Bank still stress-tests new originations. A One application is not a bypass of GDS/TDS.
If you like the all-in-one idea but want a bank you already use, compare the structure to Scotiabank STEP rather than comparing brand slogans.

faqs.question: What is Manulife One?
faqs.answer: Manulife One is an all-in-one banking and mortgage account. Deposits sit against the borrowed balance so you pay interest on the net amount, and you can usually access available credit without opening a separate HELOC application. It is more flexible than a simple closed mortgage and requires more discipline. It is optional; Manulife also offers conventional Select mortgages.

faqs.question: How does Manulife One reduce interest?
faqs.answer: Interest is charged on the outstanding net balance after deposits. A paycheque that sits in the account for two weeks before bills go out reduces interest for those days. If the account is emptied quickly, the benefit shrinks. The contract rate on each sub-account still matters; cash behaviour cannot fix a badly priced rate.

faqs.question: Does Manulife Bank offer ordinary fixed and variable mortgages?
faqs.answer: Yes. Manulife Bank Select is the conventional closed-mortgage lineup. Use that comparison if you want a standard term and payment. Use the rate table on this page for current Select and related figures from our feed.

faqs.question: Is Manulife Bank a real bank?
faqs.answer: Yes. Manulife Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank regulated by OSFI, separate from Manulife's insurance business even though it is part of the same group. Deposits are eligible for CDIC coverage within CDIC rules. A Manulife One account is still a mortgage product with credit approval, not an investment return.

faqs.question: Who should not choose Manulife One?
faqs.answer: Borrowers who keep almost no cash in the account, who want the lowest possible 5-year closed rate from a brokered monoline, or who prefer not to mix daily spending with their mortgage. Also anyone who would fail the stress test—One does not waive federal qualification on a new purchase or refinance.

faqs.question: Are Manulife's advertised rates the same as posted rates?
faqs.answer: Not always. Manulife shows posted tables and promotional or high-ratio specials with conditions. Compare the specific product (One vs Select, fixed vs variable, insured vs uninsured) to the live matrix on this page. We do not invent a 'today's best Manulife rate' in this article.

Their mortgage specialists are known for personalized service and the ability to structure financing for complex situations, including self-employed borrowers and investment properties. Laurentian's digital tools and competitive rates make it a solid choice for homeowners in Eastern Canada looking for an alternative to the major banks.

butlermortgage.name: Butler Mortgage

Butler provides competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates with a focus on transparent, honest advice. Their direct-to-consumer model, combined with deep broker expertise, gives borrowers the best of both worlds: low rates and expert guidance. Butler Mortgage is known for fast approvals, straightforward terms, and a commitment to helping Ontario homeowners find the right financing solution.

cmls.name: CMLS Financial
cmls.tagline: Commercial and residential mortgage expertise since 1974.
cmls.overview: CMLS Financial is one of Canada's oldest and most respected mortgage lenders, with over 50 years of experience in residential, commercial, and construction financing. CMLS offers competitive fixed and variable mortgage rates through the broker channel, backed by institutional-grade stability and service. Their residential mortgage products include conventional and high-ratio options, with flexible terms and prepayment privileges. CMLS is particularly strong in multi-unit residential and commercial lending, making them a preferred partner for investors and developers. Their long track record and conservative approach provide borrowers with confidence and reliability.

rfa.name: RFA (Robinson Financial Advisory)
rfa.tagline: Alternative mortgage solutions for non-traditional borrowers.
rfa.overview: RFA is a Canadian alternative mortgage lender specializing in residential mortgages for borrowers who need flexible solutions beyond what traditional banks offer. RFA provides first and second mortgages, home equity loans, and refinancing options with a focus on quick turnaround times and common-sense underwriting. They serve borrowers with bruised credit, self-employed income, or unique property types that may not fit bank guidelines. Through the broker channel, RFA offers personalized mortgage solutions with competitive alternative rates.

meridian.name: Meridian Credit Union
meridian.tagline: Ontario's largest credit union, owned by the people it serves.
meridian.overview: Meridian Credit Union is Ontario's largest credit union, serving over 370,000 members with a full range of mortgage products and financial services. As a member-owned cooperative, Meridian returns profits to members through better mortgage rates, lower fees, and community investment. Meridian offers fixed-rate, variable-rate, and home equity line of credit mortgages with flexible terms and generous prepayment options. Their Maximum Mortgage program allows borrowers to bundle multiple products for additional rate discounts. Meridian's mortgage advisors provide personalized, local service with the financial strength of one of Canada's strongest credit unions.

vancity.name: Vancity
vancity.tagline: Values-based banking for a sustainable future.
vancity.overview: Vancity is Canada's largest community credit union, serving the Vancouver area and beyond with values-based banking and competitive mortgage products. Vancity offers fixed-rate, variable-rate, and home equity mortgages, along with unique programs like the Mixer Mortgage that combines fixed and variable portions. As a certified B Corporation, Vancity invests 30% of net profits back into community programs and environmental initiatives. Their mortgage advisors provide personalized guidance with a focus on financial well-being, not just transactions. For British Columbia homeowners who want their mortgage to align with their values, Vancity is an exceptional choice.
uniqueFeatures: Largest community credit union in Canada

desjardins.name: Desjardins
desjardins.tagline: North America's largest federation of credit unions.
desjardins.overview: Desjardins is North America's largest federation of credit unions and Quebec's dominant financial institution, serving over 7 million members. Desjardins offers a comprehensive range of mortgage products including fixed-rate, variable-rate, and all-in-one mortgages through the DuoLine home equity line of credit. Their mortgage specialists provide bilingual service and deep expertise in Quebec's unique real estate market. Desjardins is known for competitive rates, flexible terms, and a strong commitment to member satisfaction. With extensive branch networks across Quebec and Ontario, Desjardins combines the personalized service of a credit union with the scale of a major financial institution.
specialties: DuoLine home equity line of credit
uniqueFeatures: Largest credit union federation in North America

coastcapital.name: Coast Capital Savings
coastcapital.tagline: Member-owned banking with simple, straightforward mortgages.
coastcapital.overview: Coast Capital Savings is Canada's largest federal credit union by membership, serving British Columbia with simple, member-focused banking and mortgage solutions. Coast Capital offers fixed-rate, variable-rate, and home equity line of credit mortgages with competitive rates and no hidden fees. Their mortgage specialists provide personalized advice with a focus on simplicity and transparency. Coast Capital is known for its community investment programs and straightforward approach to lending, making homeownership accessible for a wide range of borrowers across British Columbia.
uniqueFeatures: Largest federal credit union by membership

atb.name: ATB Financial
atb.tagline: Alberta's financial institution, built for Albertans.
atb.seoTitle: ATB Mortgage Rates Alberta | Current Fixed & Variable
atb.seoDescription: See current ATB mortgage rates for Alberta—fixed, variable, and HELOC. Compare ATB Financial offers for Calgary, Edmonton, and across the province.
atb.overview:
ATB Financial is Alberta's provincially owned financial institution—a Crown corporation of the Government of Alberta, not one of the federally chartered Big Five banks. It takes deposits and makes loans for Albertans, with a branch and advisor network that is meant to cover Calgary, Edmonton, smaller cities, and rural communities, including agricultural borrowers that national banks sometimes treat as a specialty file.

ATB offers closed fixed and variable residential mortgages and home equity lines of credit. Because it is provincially regulated, its uninsured underwriting can differ from OSFI Guideline B-20 even though insured (high-ratio) mortgages still have to satisfy CMHC, Sagen, or Canada Guaranty—including a qualifying-rate test. Alberta buyers also skip provincial land transfer tax; estimate remaining cash to close with the closing costs calculator after you pick a price.
uniqueFeatures: Wholly owned by Province of Alberta
atb.whoItsFor:
ATB is for people whose home and banking life are in Alberta: city purchases in Calgary or Edmonton, smaller centres, and rural or farm properties where local knowledge of land, income, and seasonal cash flow matters. If you do not live in Alberta and are not buying there, ATB is generally the wrong lender to pursue.

Choose ATB when you want an Alberta-based advisor, possibly a HELOC, or an agricultural/rural discussion that a Toronto call centre will not own. Choose a national bank or a brokered monoline when you need a lender that follows you to another province or when a broker can show a clearly lower insured 5-year on the same file. Run the stress test calculator anyway—insurers still apply GDS/TDS on high-ratio deals.

products.title: Residential fixed-rate mortgages
products.description: Closed fixed terms for Alberta purchases, transfers, and refinances. Compare ATB's 5-year fixed row in the table above with other lenders on the 5-year fixed hub, matching insured vs uninsured.

products.title: Residential variable-rate mortgages
products.description: Prime-linked variables. Alberta's oil-and-rate cycles make some buyers prefer a fixed payment; others want the variable. Qualification on insured deals still uses a stress-test rate, not prime.

products.title: Home equity line of credit
products.description: A HELOC against Alberta property, subject to ATB's LTV and income rules. Useful for renovations or bridging, not as a substitute for comparing a full refinance with the refinance calculator.

products.title: Rural and agricultural lending
products.description: ATB is unusually willing, relative to a typical Big Five retail desk, to talk through farm and rural files. These are underwritten on ATB's own programs. Do not assume a city residential rate card applies unchanged to a quarter section.

atb.howRatesCompare:
ATB prices for the Alberta market. It is not automatically cheaper or more expensive than RBC, TD, or a monoline on every term. Some weeks a Big Five special in Calgary undercuts ATB; some files (rural, relationship, uninsured conventional) look better in-house. The only honest comparison is the live matrix on this page versus 5-year fixed and variable tables, using the same insured/uninsured label.

Do not paste a rate into this article. Posted vs special still matters: ask which column you were quoted. Alberta's lack of land transfer tax does not change the interest rate, but it does change total cash to close relative to Ontario or B.C. on the same price.
shoppingTips: Confirm you are eligible as an Alberta resident or Alberta property buyer before you spend time on an application.
Ask whether the quote is insured or uninsured and whether it is a special or a posted rate. Match that row to this page's table.
On high-ratio deals, expect insurer rules (including a qualifying rate). ATB's provincial status does not waive CMHC/Sagen/Canada Guaranty.
For rural or agricultural property, bring income evidence the way ATB's ag desk asks for it—T4-only worksheets often undershoot farm files.
Budget closing cash without provincial land transfer tax, but still include legal, registration, and inspection. Use the closing costs calculator with province set to Alberta.
Get ATB's number in writing, then compare Calgary or Edmonton pages and the national rate table. Relationship and local turnaround can matter as much as 5 basis points.

faqs.question: Can I get an ATB mortgage if I do not live in Alberta?
faqs.answer: ATB Financial is built for Albertans and Alberta property. If you live in another province and are not buying in Alberta, you should look at national banks, credit unions in your province, or brokered lenders instead. Eligibility for specific programs is ATB's to confirm.

faqs.question: Is ATB a bank?
faqs.answer: ATB is a financial institution wholly owned by the Province of Alberta. It is not a federal Schedule I bank like TD or Manulife Bank. It still offers deposits, mortgages, and other retail products under Alberta's regulatory framework. Deposit protection follows Alberta's arrangements for ATB, not CDIC in the same way as a Schedule I bank.

faqs.question: Does ATB use the federal mortgage stress test?
faqs.answer: Insured (high-ratio) mortgages must meet default-insurer rules, which include qualifying at a stress-test rate. Uninsured mortgages at a provincially regulated lender can follow that lender's own policy, which may look similar to OSFI B-20 or may differ. Ask ATB which qualifying rate they will use on your file, and run our stress test calculator as a conservative check.

faqs.question: Does Alberta have land transfer tax?
faqs.answer: No provincial land transfer tax. Buyers still pay land-titles registration, legal fees, and the usual inspections. That is one reason cash to close in Calgary or Edmonton can be lower than on the same price in Toronto or Vancouver. Use the closing costs calculator with Alberta selected.

faqs.question: How do ATB mortgage rates compare with the big banks?
faqs.answer: It depends on the week, the term, and insured vs uninsured. ATB sometimes matches or beats a Big Five special in Alberta and sometimes does not. Use the live ATB table on this page and the national 5-year fixed hub. We do not publish a made-up ATB average in this article.

faqs.question: Can ATB help with a farm or rural property?
faqs.answer: Agricultural and rural lending is one of ATB's stated strengths. Those files are not the same as a Calgary condo purchase: income, security, and amortization can follow different programs. Speak to an ATB advisor who handles that book rather than shopping only the residential rate cards shown here.

equitable.name: Equitable Bank
equitable.tagline: Canada's Challenger Bank with big bank alternatives.
equitable.overview: Equitable Bank is Canada's seventh-largest bank by assets and the country's leading challenger bank, offering residential and commercial mortgage solutions outside the traditional banking model. Equitable provides conventional and alternative mortgages through the broker channel, including products for prime borrowers, near-prime borrowers, and those requiring specialized financing. Their EQ Bank digital platform offers some of Canada's best savings rates alongside mortgage products. Equitable is known for fast, flexible underwriting, competitive rates, and a tech-forward approach that challenges the status quo of Canadian mortgage lending.

hometrust.name: Home Trust
hometrust.tagline: Flexible mortgage solutions for Canadians who think outside the box.
hometrust.overview: Home Trust is one of Canada's leading alternative mortgage lenders, specializing in residential mortgages for borrowers who don't fit the traditional bank profile. Home Trust offers prime, near-prime, and alternative mortgage products, including first and second mortgages, with a focus on common-sense underwriting. They serve self-employed individuals, investors, newcomers to Canada, and those rebuilding credit. Home Trust's products are available exclusively through mortgage brokers, ensuring borrowers receive personalized advice alongside flexible financing solutions. With a long track record and strong capital position, Home Trust is a reliable alternative to conventional mortgage lending.
uniqueFeatures: Long track record in alternative lending

truenorth.name: True North Mortgage
truenorth.overview: True North Mortgage is one of Canada's most popular mortgage brokerages, famous for its Lowest Rate Guarantee and volume-based discounting that delivers some of the best mortgage rates in the country. True North operates as a high-volume mortgage brokerage with both online and in-person service across Canada. They offer fixed-rate, variable-rate, and specialized mortgage products from a wide range of lenders including banks, monolines, and credit unions. True North's straightforward approach, transparent pricing, and commitment to beating competitors' rates have made them a favourite among rate-savvy Canadian homeowners.
uniqueFeatures: Access to bank, monoline, and credit union lenders
